title: One Ratio, Two Keepers
endLine: pH follows one ratio: lungs hold the bottom, kidneys rebuild the top.

scenes.tts: An adult's plasma at rest holds only about forty nanomoles of free hydrogen ions per litre. Metabolism adds acid every day, yet p H stays near seven point four. What holds it there?
scenes.narration: An adult's plasma at rest holds only about 40 nanomoles of free hydrogen ions per litre. Metabolism adds acid every day, yet pH stays near 7.4. What holds it there?
scenes.caption: An adult's plasma at rest holds only about 40 nanomoles of free hydrogen ions per litre. Metabolism adds acid every day, yet pH stays near 7.4. What holds it there?
scenes.visual: THE WORLD, built here and kept for the whole film and the next (16:9). COLOUR BY CONCEPT, same in every scene: bicarbonate (the base) BLUE fluid and BLUE dots; dissolved carbon dioxide (the acid) ORANGE fluid and ORANGE bubbles; added acid (hydrogen ions) RED dots; the pH gauge and its needle bright WHITE; the lungs PINK; the kidney PURPLE. LAYOUT: CENTRE, filling about 70% of frame height, a big fraction made of two clear tanks on one shared vertical scale: an upper tank of BLUE fluid labelled 'bicarbonate', a thick WHITE fraction bar, and a lower tank of ORANGE fluid labelled 'dissolved CO2'. Each tank holds 50 mmol/L when full (scale hidden, no numbers on the tanks); fluid heights are always drawn in proportion to concentration, so at rest the BLUE fluid fills 24/50 of its tank and the ORANGE fluid only 1.2/50 of its tank, a thin layer. LEFT: a PINK pair of lungs beside the lower tank, joined to it by a short tube, breathing slowly (a gentle swell every 4 s); a PURPLE kidney beside the upper tank, joined to it by a tube. Both organs start dim. RIGHT: a tall vertical pH gauge, scale 6.0 to 7.6, ticks every 0.2, a bright tick at 7.40. The WHITE needle is ALWAYS computed from the drawn levels: pH = 6.1 + log10(upper level / lower level). Hook motion: RED dots rain slowly into the upper tank from the top of the frame, label 'acid, every day'; faint ORANGE bubbles drift out through the lung tube; the needle trembles at 7.40 but holds. A small counter at top right: 'free H+: 40 nmol/L'. On the question, white text across the top: 'What holds pH there?'

Title 'One Ratio, Two Keepers' fades in across the top for 2 s while the question text fades out. The RED rain thins to a stop; BLUE dots keep drifting in the upper tank and ORANGE bubbles shimmer in the thin lower layer. Lungs keep their slow swell.

scenes.tts: Picture p H as the reading of a fraction. On top, bicarbonate, the base: twenty-four millimoles per litre. Below, dissolved carbon dioxide, the acid: one point two. That is twenty to one.
scenes.narration: Picture pH as the reading of a fraction. On top, bicarbonate, the base: 24 millimoles per litre. Below, dissolved carbon dioxide, the acid: 1.2. That is 20 to 1.
scenes.caption: Picture pH as the reading of a fraction. On top, bicarbonate, the base: 24 millimoles per litre. Below, dissolved carbon dioxide, the acid: 1.2. That is 20 to 1.
scenes.visual: On 'fraction', the WHITE fraction bar brightens and the gauge needle pulses once at 7.40. On 'bicarbonate', the BLUE fluid brightens and gets the label '24 mmol/L'. On 'dissolved carbon dioxide', the thin ORANGE layer brightens and gets the label '1.2 mmol/L'. On 'twenty to one', a large WHITE '20 : 1' appears on the fraction bar. A small tag at bottom right, 'human plasma, 37 C', appears and stays all film.

scenes.tts: In human plasma, p H is six point one plus the log of that ratio. Log twenty is one point three, so p H is seven point four.
scenes.narration: In human plasma, pH is 6.1 plus the log of that ratio. Log 20 is 1.3, so pH is 7.4.
scenes.caption: In human plasma, pH is 6.1 plus the log of that ratio. Log 20 is 1.3, so pH is 7.4.
scenes.visual: Under the gauge, a WHITE line builds: 'pH = 6.1 + log(ratio)'. On 'the log of twenty', it transforms to 'pH = 6.1 + 1.30', then to 'pH = 7.40', and the needle glows at its 7.40 tick. BLUE dots keep drifting; ORANGE bubbles keep shimmering; lungs keep breathing.

scenes.tts: Double both terms, and p H does not move. Halve the top alone, and p H falls to seven point one. p H follows the ratio, not either number.
scenes.narration: Double both terms, and pH does not move. Halve the top alone, and pH falls to 7.1. pH follows the ratio, not either number.
scenes.caption: Double both terms, and pH does not move. Halve the top alone, and pH falls to 7.1. pH follows the ratio, not either number.
scenes.visual: On 'double both', both fluids rise together to twice their height (BLUE to 48/50 of its tank, ORANGE to 2.4/50); the '20 : 1' stays and the needle stays at 7.40. Both ease back to 24 and 1.2. On 'halve the top alone', the BLUE fluid drains to 12 (label '12'); '20 : 1' morphs to '10 : 1'; the needle slides down to 7.10 (6.1 + log10 10), label '7.10'. On 'follows the ratio', the BLUE fluid refills to 24, '20 : 1' returns and the needle climbs back to 7.40.

scenes.tts: A puzzle: the pair's p K is six point one, well below seven point four. Seal bicarbonate in a bottle and add acid. Each proton turns a bicarbonate into carbon dioxide. The small bottom term grows fast, and p H crashes.
scenes.narration: A puzzle: the pair's pK is 6.1, well below 7.4. Seal bicarbonate in a bottle and add acid. Each proton turns a bicarbonate into carbon dioxide. The small bottom term grows fast, and pH crashes.
scenes.caption: A puzzle: the pair's pK is 6.1, well below 7.4. Seal bicarbonate in a bottle and add acid. Each proton turns a bicarbonate into carbon dioxide. The small bottom term grows fast, and pH crashes.
scenes.visual: On 'p K', a dim tick at 6.1 on the gauge gets the label 'pK 6.1', with a bracket up to 7.40 labelled '1.3 below'. On 'seal', a glass lid slides over both tanks and a small clamp closes the lung tube; the lungs keep breathing but no bubbles pass. On 'add acid', a burst of RED dots falls into the upper tank (animator's hidden dose: 5 mmol/L on the tank scale; show no dose number). Each RED dot that meets a BLUE dot turns the pair into one ORANGE bubble that sinks into the lower tank. The BLUE level falls a little (24 to 19); the ORANGE layer climbs to about five times its height (1.2 to 6.2). On 'p H crashes', the needle drops fast to its computed value (about 6.6) with no number shown. Tag under the tanks: 'schematic dose'. The '20 : 1' label fades out.

scenes.tts: Closed, this would be a poor buffer. So how can the same pair be the main buffer of the fluid outside your cells?
scenes.narration: Closed, this would be a poor buffer. So how can the same pair be the main buffer of the fluid outside your cells?
scenes.caption: Closed, this would be a poor buffer. So how can the same pair be the main buffer of the fluid outside your cells?
scenes.visual: The sealed state holds: lid on, lung tube clamped, ORANGE layer swollen, needle low. On 'poor buffer', a WHITE label 'closed: poor buffer' appears on the lid. On the question, white question card across the top: 'A poor buffer, yet the main one?'

Predict pause. The question card stays. Near-stillness by design: the lungs keep their slow swell behind the clamped tube, ORANGE bubbles jostle in the swollen lower layer, the needle trembles at its low reading.

scenes.tts: Because the body is open. The lungs breathe the new carbon dioxide away. So the bottom term stays put, and only the top shrinks.
scenes.narration: Because the body is open. The lungs breathe the new carbon dioxide away. So the bottom term stays put, and only the top shrinks.
scenes.caption: Because the body is open. The lungs breathe the new carbon dioxide away. So the bottom term stays put, and only the top shrinks.
scenes.visual: Question card dissolves. Rewind smoothly to rest (24 over 1.2, needle 7.40), then the lid lifts away and the lung clamp opens; the lungs brighten to full PINK, label 'open'. The same RED burst falls (same hidden dose). Each RED dot meeting a BLUE dot still makes an ORANGE bubble, but on each breath the bubbles rise up the tube and out through the lungs, label 'CO2 out'. A dashed line marks the 1.2 level of the ORANGE layer, which stays on it. On 'only the top shrinks', the BLUE level falls from 24 to 19 and the needle dips only slightly, to its computed value (about 7.30), no number shown. Tag 'schematic dose' stays.

scenes.tts: Measure buffering as acid needed per unit fall in p H. Open, the pair manages about fifty-five millimoles per litre. Sealed, about two point six: roughly twentyfold.
scenes.narration: Measure buffering as acid needed per unit fall in pH. Open, the pair manages about 55 millimoles per litre. Sealed, about 2.6: roughly twentyfold.
scenes.caption: Measure buffering as acid needed per unit fall in pH. Open, the pair manages about 55 millimoles per litre. Sealed, about 2.6: roughly twentyfold.
scenes.visual: The kidney dims further and the gauge slides a little right to make room. Beside the tanks, two vertical bars grow from a shared baseline, heights in exact proportion 55 : 2.6. Axis label 'acid per pH unit'. On 'open', a tall BLUE-outlined bar with the open-lung icon, labelled 'open: 55'. On 'sealed', a short bar with the lid icon, labelled 'sealed: 2.6'. On 'twentyfold', a WHITE bracket between their tops, labelled 'about x20'. Lungs keep breathing ORANGE bubbles out.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. p H follows one ratio, bicarbonate over dissolved carbon dioxide. The lungs hold the bottom, starting within minutes. The kidney sets the top, over days.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. pH follows one ratio, bicarbonate over dissolved carbon dioxide. The lungs hold the bottom, starting within minutes. The kidney sets the top, over days.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea. pH follows one ratio, bicarbonate over dissolved carbon dioxide. The lungs hold the bottom, starting within minutes. The kidney sets the top, over days.
scenes.visual: The bars fade; the gauge slides back. The tanks keep the post-acid state (BLUE at 19, ORANGE on its 1.2 line, needle at its computed reading just below 7.40). On 'one ratio', the WHITE fraction bar glows. On 'the lungs hold the bottom', the lungs and the lung tube pulse PINK and a stopwatch icon appears beside them, label 'minutes'. On 'the kidney sets the top', the kidney brightens to full PURPLE, its tube to the upper tank pulses, and a calendar icon appears beside it, label 'days'. Text at the top: 'One ratio, two keepers'.

scenes.tts: But buffering is not removal. Sulfuric acid from sulfur-containing amino acids cannot be breathed off. Its protons stay in the body. The bicarbonate they spent is gone until the kidney makes more.
scenes.narration: But buffering is not removal. Sulfuric acid from sulfur-containing amino acids cannot be breathed off. Its protons stay in the body. The bicarbonate they spent is gone until the kidney makes more.
scenes.caption: But buffering is not removal. Sulfuric acid from sulfur-containing amino acids cannot be breathed off. Its protons stay in the body. The bicarbonate they spent is gone until the kidney makes more.
scenes.visual: The icons fade. The RED dots from the acid burst gather into a shallow RED tray under the tanks, label 'still in the body'; on 'sulfuric acid', a tag 'sulfuric acid' sits on the tray. ORANGE bubbles keep leaving through the lungs, but no RED dot leaves that way. On 'the bicarbonate they spent', a dashed BLUE line marks the old 24 level above the lowered BLUE fluid (19), and the gap between them is shaded and labelled 'spent'. On 'until the kidney makes more', the kidney pulses.

scenes.tts: Human kidneys have two jobs. They filter about four thousand millimoles of bicarbonate a day, roughly eighty times the day's acid. Job one is to take it back: one vanishes from the tubule, one appears in the blood. No new base is made.
scenes.narration: Human kidneys have two jobs. They filter about 4,000 millimoles of bicarbonate a day, roughly eighty times the day's acid. Job one is to take it back: one vanishes from the tubule, one appears in the blood. No new base is made.
scenes.caption: Human kidneys have two jobs. They filter about 4,000 millimoles of bicarbonate a day, roughly eighty times the day's acid. Job one is to take it back: one vanishes from the tubule, one appears in the blood. No new base is made.
scenes.visual: The lungs dim (still breathing). The PURPLE kidney grows into a simple schematic tubule: a U-shaped PURPLE tube beside the upper tank, its wall drawn as a row of pale cells, with the tank side marked 'blood'. A steady BLUE stream flows from the tank into the tubule, label 'filtered'. On 'four thousand', two side-by-side bars appear at the top left: a tall BLUE bar 'about 4,000 a day' and a RED bar beside it exactly 1/80 its height, 'day's acid: about 50'. On 'take it back', BLUE dots return from the tubule to the tank. On 'one vanishes', one highlighted BLUE dot inside the tubule fades out as a fresh BLUE dot appears on the blood side of the wall and drops into the tank; a dashed WHITE arc joins the two, label 'indirect route'. On 'no new base', the bars fade and the shaded 'spent' gap pulses: the BLUE level is still at 19.

scenes.tts: Job two repays the debt. Making new bicarbonate, by excreting acid, is the only way. Some acid leaves riding on phosphate. Most leaves as ammonium, made from glutamine.
scenes.narration: Job two repays the debt. Making new bicarbonate, by excreting acid, is the only way. Some acid leaves riding on phosphate. Most leaves as ammonium, made from glutamine.
scenes.caption: Job two repays the debt. Making new bicarbonate, by excreting acid, is the only way. Some acid leaves riding on phosphate. Most leaves as ammonium, made from glutamine.
scenes.visual: A small droplet labelled 'urine' hangs from the end of the tubule. RED dots leave the 'still in the body' tray, enter the tubule and travel to the urine droplet. On 'phosphate', a few ride on TEAL carrier shapes labelled 'phosphate'. On 'ammonium', more are packed into GOLD tokens labelled 'ammonium', which spring from a GOLD 'glutamine' token set in the tubule wall; GOLD tokens outnumber TEAL carriers (proportions schematic). For every RED dot that reaches the urine, one new BLUE dot drops into the upper tank: the 'spent' gap closes, the BLUE level climbs back to the dashed 24 line, the tray empties and the needle returns to 7.40 (computed).

scenes.tts: So the ratio holds, and an ordinary pair guards the blood. Breathing clears the new carbon dioxide within minutes, and the kidney repays the spent base over days.
scenes.narration: So the ratio holds, and an ordinary pair guards the blood. Breathing clears the new carbon dioxide within minutes, and the kidney repays the spent base over days.
scenes.caption: So the ratio holds, and an ordinary pair guards the blood. Breathing clears the new carbon dioxide within minutes, and the kidney repays the spent base over days.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full world: tanks at 24 over 1.2, '20 : 1' back on the fraction bar, needle steady at 7.40. The gentle RED rain of the hook resumes. On 'breathing clears', ORANGE bubbles stream out through the bright PINK lungs (stopwatch 'minutes' returns). On 'the kidney repays', the PURPLE tubule sends RED dots to the urine droplet and BLUE dots into the upper tank (calendar 'days' returns). Both organs then breathe and work together while the needle holds.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (RED rain falling, ORANGE bubbles leaving through the lungs, BLUE dots returning from the kidney, needle steady at 7.40). Large white text, centred: 'pH follows one ratio: lungs hold the bottom, kidneys rebuild the top.'
